title: "BIO 5150L Resources and Tutorials"
---

### [Download a .R script organization template](downloads/Organized_Script.R){download="Organized_Script.R"}

- You can download and then use this template as a starting point for new R scripts and as a guide for organizing your code.

### [Using Git & GitHub Tutorial](https://claisselab.github.io/BIO_5100/git_github_rstudio.html)

- Guides you through installing (software) Git on your computer, creating a GitHub.com account, connecting it to RStudio, and creating a repository (i.e., a folder).

- Describes workflows for personal version control, student–PI code review, and publicly sharing analysis code.

- Provides guidance for organizing projects, excluding and backing up data, and other uses, issues, and organization.

### [Multivariate Module](https://claisselab.github.io/BIO_5100/Multivariate_module.html)

Tutorials and resources for preparing, visualizing, and analyzing multivariate ecological data.

- Summarizing and exploring multivariate data
- nMDS ordination and PERMANOVA for community composition
- PCA for continuous environmental, morphological, or physiological variables
- Hierarchical cluster analysis for species assemblages or continuous variables

### [Generalized Linear Models (GLMs) Module](https://claisselab.github.io/BIO_5100/GLM_module.html) *(in development)*

A developing set of resources and tutorials for fitting and interpreting generalized linear models in R.

- Overview of common GLM distributions and link functions
- Poisson and negative binomial regression for biological count data
- Model diagnostics using DHARMa and model comparison using AICc
- Interpreting and plotting predictions, estimated means, response ratios, confidence intervals, and interactions
- R code that can be adapted for analyzing your own count data
